artifacts.title: Position-aware GBM beats one-hot ridge on TEM-1 (Stiffler 2015) DMS
artifacts.summary: Features: leave-one-out position mean of training DMS scores, positional window means (+-1, +-3), std at position, Kyte-Doolittle and volume of wt/mut residues, one-hot mut and wt. Model: HistGradientBoosting with absolute-error loss, trained on train.csv only. 5-fold CV on the public train set: MAE 0.375 vs 0.602 for the one-hot ridge baseline (exec-a86dd0cc). The held-out branch was checked on a simulated inputs file built from training rows; no held-out labels were used.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.1983, 95% CI [-0.2239, -0.1752], beyond the minimum effect 0.0114)

claim.statement: On BLAT_ECOLX_Stiffler_2015, a position-aware gradient-boosted model trained on train.csv achieves lower held-out MAE than the one-hot ridge baseline.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before planning anything. I'll read the guide, the command list, and the data READMEs.
Next I'll read the data READMEs, the baseline README and script, and the lab's GUIDE. The baseline tells me what I have to beat.

The baseline is one-hot plus ridge. A position-level model (per-position mean of training scores, plus mutant amino-acid properties) should beat it on held-out variants. Before writing anything, I need the baseline's invocation and the train file's columns.

I'll start with a position-aware model on the Stiffler DMS. The baseline is one-hot ridge, which ignores that a position's average substitution effect carries most of the signal. I'll compare against that baseline under 5-fold CV on the public train set before any held-out claim.


```bash
mkdir -p /work/pos && cd /work/pos && cat > run.py <<'EOF'
import os, glob, json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold
AA = "ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY"
KD = dict(A=1.8,R=-4.5,N=-3.5,D=-
Write the position-aware model to a file, then run the 5-fold CV comparison against the ridge baseline through `lab exec`.
Fix the path handling and rerun the CV comparison. The held-out branch will look up `$EVAL_DIR/<id>/inputs.*` using the id from `meta.json`.
Inspect `$DATA_DIR` and `$EVAL_DIR` inside a recorded exec so I stop guessing at the layout.
Fix the data root so `train.csv` and `meta.json` come from the dataset subfolder, then run the recorded CV comparison against the ridge baseline.
Test the EVAL branch locally on a fake held-out file so the evaluator's run does not fail on a path or column error.
Read the artifact schema so the finding JSON matches it, then publish with the recorded CV exec as evidence.

Publish a finding that the position-aware model beats the ridge baseline on the Stiffler held-out set. Evidence is exec-a86dd0cc, whose metrics.json contains both MAE values, and the test runs the same code on `$EVAL_DIR`.

Patch `parse` to fall back to a sequence-vs-wild-type diff, re-run the recorded CV exec on the patched code, and store the code as a blob for teammates. Then check the simulated held-out branch with a sequence-only inputs file.

The evaluator re-runs the code blob named in `test.code`, so that blob must be the one that handles sequence-only inputs. I'll contribute a replacement finding with blob 1513fe… and evidence exec-645fb802, whose metrics match exec-a86dd0cc.

One founder cannot cover five other assays well. I'll recruit two researchers with separate dataset sets, post the shared script and its pitfalls (the DATA_DIR layout, the sequence-only inputs, the flawed v1 blob), and ask them to publish `prediction` findings with CV evidence.

Founder here. Shared method: /work/pos/run.py (position-aware GBM; blob 1513fe41…). Pitfalls: (1) inside lab exec, $DATA_DIR is the root /lab/data, NOT the dataset folder, so set DATA=os.path.join(DATA_DIR, DSID). (2) Held-out inputs may have only id+sequence; parse() must derive the mutation from the sequence (already fixed in v2). (3) My first finding findin-7e40f3f3 points at the old blob 6231495… that cannot read sequence-only inputs; use findin-bc54e2a2 instead. Please report CV numbers from lab exec only.
I'll start by reading the lab guide and the founder's GBM script, then the README for the RASK datasets, before changing anything.
I'll start by reading the lab guide and the founder's script so I know the required formats and what I'm copying.
I need the README for the RASK datasets to get the WT sequence and data layout, and to see the head of run.py (the truncated part, including the parse function and how sequence is read).
The output was truncated, so I need the top of run.py, the two dataset READMEs, and the baselines folder before I copy anything.

I'll copy `/work/pos` into two working directories, swap in the RASK DSID and WT sequence, and check the train.csv header and the baseline script. Then I'll run the 5-fold CV for both datasets in the background.
Both proteins need their own WT string and DSID in the copied script. I'll make two copies, check the WT lengths against the training sequences, and run 5-fold CV for each.
File a `corrects` note against findin-7e40f3f3 so the board shows which finding to use. Then pause until the recruits post.

The WT sequence and DSID are swapped in both copies, and P=200 covers the 188-residue protein. Now I'll run the 5-fold CV for each dataset through `lab exec`, which is the only thing that counts as evidence.

Both CV runs came back with the position model beating ridge (CASP3 0.426 vs 0.487; KCNE1 0.160 vs 0.206). Before publishing I need the exec IDs, the comparator in `baselines/`, and the contribution schema.

The CV results are in, but the exec IDs weren't in the truncated output. I'll pull them from `lab runs` and read the rest of the schema before writing the contribution JSON.

```bash
lab runs | head -60
echo ---
lab schema | tail -60
```

Before publishing, I need the exact contribution format, and I should verify the `EVAL_DIR` prediction branch works, since the evaluator will run that path. I'll mock a held-out input from a train subset, run locally, and check the output shape.

The CV numbers are confirmed with exec IDs: exec-b767158d (CASP3) and exec-daea5b52 (KCNE1). Before writing the contribution I need the `Test` schema fields and the prediction-mode run.

```bash
lab schema | python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps(d['\$defs'].get('Test'),indent=1)); print(json.dumps(d['\$defs'].get('Rel'),indent=1))" 2>/dev/null || lab schema | grep -n -A40 '"Test"' | head -80
echo ---
lab help | head -40
```

The prediction test needs a code blob. I'll store the CASP3 and KCNE1 copies of `run.py` with `lab put`, which the test runs with `EVAL_DIR` set. Then I'll write the two findings using the CV exec IDs and post a board note.
The test code can be the same `run.py` directory, since its `EVAL_DIR` branch writes `predictions.csv`. I'll upload each directory and read back the blob ids before writing the contribution JSON.
